experiment: P3o-E state-preserving frozen frequency delay parameter residual
research_question: Can a delay-peak parameter residual improve full twelve-parameter sensing while preserving every selected local time-frequency recognition logit and BatchNorm buffer exactly throughout residual training?
hypothesis: Keeping the complete F backbone in evaluation state during residual optimization prevents the P3o-D normalization-state leak, so any parameter change is causally confined to the posterior-conditioned delay residual.

identity_protocol.identity_pairing: receiver_noise_seed grouped across regime and power views

methods.F_base: Local STFT plus adjacent-frame phase-increment backbone, trained with BCEWithLogits plus 0.1 masked SmoothL1 and selected solely on early identities.
methods.E_state_preserving_residual: Freeze every F parameter and force the whole F module to eval whenever the side branch enters train mode. A delay-peak encoder predicts a classwise residual, multiplied by detached sigmoid(F logits), and adds it only to F parameter prediction. No recognition logit, recognition threshold, F BatchNorm buffer, or F parameter is trainable or mutable during side training.

base.checkpoint: C_joint: maximum early macro-AUPR among epochs with oracle parameter NMAE <= 1.01 times minimum

residual.checkpoint: minimum early oracle parameter NMAE; recognition path is fixed

training.calibration: Fit each F threshold vector only on its calibration identities, then reuse that vector verbatim for E. No development selection or recalibration is permitted.

decision_rule: Only if every gate passes may 1200M and 1210M be generated for two fresh confirmations. Any failure permanently stops this exact side-residual variant; no loss, width, residual scale, checkpoint, threshold, base architecture, or 1190M result may be tuned.
